entry.title: Real-rooted Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of crown posets and wheel and whirl matroids
entry.summary: We prove that the Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of crown order polytopes are real-rooted, settling a conjecture of Lundström and Saud Maia Leite. For each integer $r\ge3$, the crown order polytope on $2r$ elements and the rank-$r$ whirl base polytope have the same $h^*$-polynomial. The $h^*$-polynomials of the rank-$r$ wheel and whirl base polytopes, as well as every convex combination of the two, have $2r-2$ distinct negative roots. Their coefficient sequences are positive, unimodal, and strictly ultra log-concave of order $2r-2$.

entry.title: A Faster Auction Algorithm for Weighted Matroid Intersection
entry.summary: We consider the weighted matroid intersection problem in the independence-oracle model. A sequence of works by Huang--Kakimura--Kamiyama~[SODA'16 \& Math. Program'19], Chekuri--Quanrud~[SODA'16], Quanrud~[ICALP'24], and Dudeja--Grilnberger~[IPCO'26] has developed efficient $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithms for this problem. We present a simple deterministic auction algorithm that, given two matroids on a common ground set of size $n$, computes a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximate maximum-weight common independent set using $O(n \varepsilon^{-2} \log^2(n))$ independence-oracle queries. This is the first deterministic $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm for the weighted matroid intersection problem whose query complexity is nearly linear in $n$ and polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$. Our algorithm builds on the auction algorithm for unweighted matroid intersection by Huang--Kobayashi~['26].
entry.arxiv:comment: 17 pages. In this version, we have completely rewritten the proof, which is now simpler and easier to follow, and improved the clarity and presentation of the paper. We plan to combine this work with that of Huang and Kobayashi (arXiv:2609.38685) in a future version, providing a more polished and unified presentation

entry.title: From Linear to Polylogarithmic: Dynamic Submodular Maximization over Matroids
entry.summary: We study the problem of submodular maximization under a matroid constraint. In this problem, there is a monotone submodular function $f: 2^{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^+$ and a matroid $M(N, I)$, accessible via value and independence oracles and the goal is to find the independent set $S \in I$ maximizing the objective function, i.e., $f(S) = \max_{I \in I} f(I)$. In the fully dynamic setting, the active ground set $N \subseteq N$ evolves through element insertions and deletions. The goal is to maintain a solution $S \subseteq N$ with $S \in I$ and $f(S) = \max_{I \subseteq N,, I \in I} f(I)$ after each update. Two approximation algorithms have been proposed to solve this problem: Dütting et al. developed a $(4+ε)$-approximation algorithm with an expected amortized update time of $O\!\bigl(\frac{k^2}ε \log k \log n \log^3 \frac{k}ε\bigr)$, and Banihashem et al. achieved a similar approximation with a better update time $O\!\bigl(k \log k \log^3 \frac{k}ε\bigr)$. However, these methods both become inefficient when the rank $k$ of the matroid is large (e.g., when $k = n^{o(1)}$). The central open question in this line of work is whether a fully dynamic algorithm with polylogarithmic update time exists. We resolve this question by presenting the first fully dynamic algorithm for submodular maximization over matroids with polylogarithmic update time. Our algorithm maintains a $(4+ε)$-approximate solution with expected amortized update time $poly(\log n, ε^{-1})$, where $n = |N|$. In particular, the update time is independent of the matroid rank $k$, thereby eliminating the dependence on $k$ and settling the open problem.

entry.title: Random Deletion for Circuits in Regular Matroids
entry.summary: We study a simple random deletion algorithm to find short circuits in regular matroids. Given a regular matroid $M$ with $m$ elements, the algorithm randomly deletes each element independently with probability $1-1/m^{Θ(1/g)}$ where $g$ is the size of a minimum circuit, and returns the remaining set $R$ of elements. We establish the following results: 1. With high probability, $R$ contains no circuit and is therefore independent. 2. For every $α$-approximate minimum circuit $C$ where $α\geq 1$, with probability at least $m^{-O(α)}$, the entire circuit $C$ survives in $R$ and moreover, the minimum number of elements that need to be removed to make $R$ independent is $O(α\log(α+2))$. This yields an algorithmic proof that the number of $α$-approximate minimum circuits is $m^{O(α)}$, improving the previous known bound of $m^{O(α^2)}$ by Gurjar and Vishnoi, and resolving a recent conjecture of Khanna, Putterman, and Song. Our results yield two immediate applications. First, we obtain very simple RNC algorithms for computing the shortest circuit, and for enumerating all $α$-approximate circuits, of a regular matroid without computing the Seymour decomposition. Second, we obtain a randomized parallel algorithm to find a basis of a regular matroid under independence-oracle access. It uses polynomially many independence-oracle queries in $O(\log m)$ adaptive rounds and succeeds with high probability. This follows from the framework of Khanna, Putterman, and Song and the improved counting bound, and extends their result from graphic matroids to regular matroids.

entry.title: Proximity Theorem and FPT Algorithm for Minimum Group-labeled Matroid Bases
entry.summary: Let $M$ be a matroid, let $\ell:E(M)\to G$ be a labeling of its elements by an abelian group, and let $F\subseteq G$ be finite. A base is $F$-avoiding if the label sum of its elements is not in $F$. We prove that, for arbitrary costs, a min-cost $F$-avoiding base can be obtained from any min-cost base using at most $|F|$ exchanges. This resolves the weighted proximity conjecture by Hörsch, Imolay, Mizutani, Oki, and Schwarcz. Our main technical tool is to replace the assumption of Schrijver--Seymour Conjecture in Liu and Xu's earlier work with Kemperman--Scherk Theorem. The proximity theorem combined with approaches in earlier work gives an FPT algorithm that finds a min-cost $F$-avoiding base parameterized by $|G|$. We additionally give an FPT algorithm parameterized by $|F|$, answering a question of Hörsch et al.

entry.title: Inverse Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of matroids under deletion
entry.summary: We provide a deletion formula for the inverse Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial and the inverse $Z$-polynomial of a matroid. Our formulas provide analogues to the deletion formulas of Braden--Vysogorets for Kazhdan--Lusztig and $Z$-polynomials. We discuss several consequences, which include closed formulas and recursions for these invariants on uniform matroids, projective geometries, glued cycles, and arbitrary matroids of corank $2$. As a relevant application of our deletion formula, we show the existence of a matroid of rank $19$ which disproves a conjecture of Xie and Zhang concerning a real-rootedness property of inverse Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials.

entry.title: On $k$-connected Sets in Matroids
entry.summary: In 1966, Tutte defined $k$-connected matroids for each $k \ge 2$. Robertson and Seymour built on Tutte's idea to define tangles as a way to identify highly connected parts of a matroid. Motivated by tangles, a set $Z$ in a matroid $M$ has been defined to be $3$-connected if, for each $j$ in $\{1,2\}$, there is no $j$-separation $(X,Y)$ of $M$ such that each of $|Z \cap X|$ and $|Z \cap Y|$ is at least $j$. This paper solves a problem of Whittle for $k= 3$ by proving that a minor-minimal matroid having $Z$ as a $3$-connected set has at most $3|Z| - 4$ elements. We also identify the matroids for which this bound is attained.

entry.title: A weighted inequality for matroid flats and log-concavity of Whitney numbers
entry.summary: Using the Hodge-Riemann relations for matroid Chow rings, we establish a weighted inequality for flats of a loopless matroid. As applications, we prove the points-lines-planes conjecture and Brylawski's conjecture on the ultra-log-concavity of Whitney numbers of the first kind. We also characterize the cases of equality in both inequalities.

entry.title: A Matroidal Framework for Random Access in Linear Codes
entry.summary: We study random access in linear codes when codeword symbols are sampled independently and uniformly with replacement. A code is recovery balanced if the expected number of samples required to recover a codeword coordinate is the same for every coordinate. We express the recovery expectations in terms of the associated matroid and derive a coordinatewise identity relating these values for a code and its dual. This proves that a linear code is recovery balanced if and only if its dual is recovery balanced, establishing a conjecture of Gruica et al. We further define the recovery balance for arbitrary matroids and show that asymptotically almost every sparse paving matroid is not recovery balanced.

entry.title: A Nearly Tight Lower Bound for Matroid Intersection Prophet Inequalities
entry.summary: We study prophet inequalities under intersections of $q$ partition matroids, where an online algorithm irrevocably selects elements with independent nonnegative values drawn from known distributions and revealed in an adversarial order. We prove an $Ω(q/\log q)$ lower bound on the competitive ratio. Together with the known $O(q)$ upper bounds, this resolves, up to a logarithmic factor, the optimal dependence on $q$, an open question posed by Correa, Cristi, Fielbaum, Pollner, and Weinberg (IPCO 2022) and Saxena, Velusamy, and Weinberg (ITCS 2023). Our construction also yields an $Ω(d/\log d)$ lower bound for $d$-single-minded auctions, where buyers request fixed bundles of at most $d$ unit-capacity items. Our construction and analysis build on the big-decisions-first framework of Rubinstein and Singla (STOC 2026). Previous lower bounds for this problem hold even for i.i.d. Bernoulli values, whereas our instance uses nonidentical distributions. For i.i.d. Bernoulli values, we prove a $q^{1-o(1)}$ lower bound, improving the previous $q^{1/2+Ω(1/\log\log q)}$ of Saxena, Velusamy, and Weinber (ITCS 2023). To this end, we construct $p^p$ pairwise qualitatively independent partitions into $p$ blocks on a ground set of only $p^{2+o(1)}$ points.

entry.title: On minimum-size matroid counterexamples to the multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality
entry.summary: Let $M$ be a matroid and let $\Tutte_M(x,y)$ be its Tutte polynomial. The multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality \[ \Tutte_M(2,0)\Tutte_M(0,2)\geq \Tutte_M(1,1)^2 \] was proved to be false for matroids by Beke, Csáji, Csikvári, and Pituk (\emph{Adv. Math.} \textbf{446} (2024), 109674). Let $U_{n,r}$ denote the rank-$r$ uniform matroid on $n$ elements, where $0<r<n$, and let $U_{n,r}^{(q)}$ denote the matroid obtained by replacing each element of $U_{n,r}$ with $q$ parallel copies. They constructed an infinite family of counterexamples of the form $U_{n,r}^{(2)}$, including $U_{33,22}^{(2)}$. In this paper, we prove that every $U_{n,r}^{(q)}$ with $q\geq3$ satisfies the inequality. For $q=2$, we prove that the minimum number of elements in such a counterexample is $62$, attained by $U_{31,21}^{(2)}$. For loopless and bridgeless graphs, Noble and Royle (\emph{Eur. J. Comb.} \textbf{38} (2014), 24--35) showed that every edge of a minimum-size counterexample to the multiplicative Merino--Welsh conjecture lies in a series or parallel class of size two or three. For matroids, we further prove that every element of a minimum-size loopless and coloopless counterexample lies in exactly one series or parallel class of size two.

entry.title: On Hankel Determinantal Matroids
entry.summary: We initiate a study of the algebraic matroid associated to the ideal generated by the $(r+1)$-minors of a Hankel matrix of variables. We prove that this matroid is uniform, that is, a coordinate projection from the corresponding Hankel determinantal variety is generically finite if and only if it preserves at least $2r$ anti-diagonals. For such projections, we establish bounds on the degree. These results are of significance to the problem of Hankel low-rank matrix completion.
